title: Affine perfect extension after adjoining a shift
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U be a quasi-compact open of X, and let F be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then there exists a perfect object E of D(\mathcal O_X) whose restriction to U is isomorphic to F \oplus F[1].

proof.text: By [lem-sc-affine-perfect-plus-locally-free], choose an integer r, a finite locally free module \mathcal F on U, and a perfect object E of D(\mathcal O_X) whose restriction is isomorphic to \mathcal F[-r]\oplus F.

source.place: Tag 08EI proof, first paragraph, invoking Tag 08ED

proof.text: The perfect object E lies in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]: locally it is isomorphic to a strictly perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex], a bounded complex of finite locally free modules, whose cohomology sheaves are kernels modulo images of maps of quasi-coherent modules, hence quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherence is local. So [lem-sc-affine-perfect-map-lift] applies with A=E and E'=E to the endomorphism of E|_U that is the identity on the summand \mathcal F[-r] and zero on the summand F (defined through the chosen isomorphism of Step 1). It gives a perfect E_1 and maps E\xleftarrow{\beta}E_1\xrightarrow{\gamma}E with \beta an isomorphism on U and \gamma|_U\circ(\beta|_U)^{-1} equal to this endomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08EI proof, second paragraph, invoking Tag 08EH

proof.text: Let C=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma), so E_1\to E\to C\to E_1[1] is a distinguished triangle; since E_1 and E are perfect, C is perfect [lem-pc-perfect-two-out-of-three]. Restriction to U is a triangulated functor, so C|_U\cong\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma|_U). On U, identify E_1 with E using \beta; then \gamma|_U becomes the projection \mathrm{id}\oplus 0 on \mathcal F[-r]\oplus F, whose cone is \operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F[-r]})\oplus\operatorname{Cone}(0:F\to F)\cong 0\oplus(F\oplus F[1]). Thus C|_U\simeq F\oplus F[1].
